implementation_constraints: two units: source/model.py (pure) + source/cli.py (entry, imports model); run python cli.py from source/

unresolved_intent.decision: An id is marked as seen the moment the posting is first encountered — including when that first occurrence is itself rejected for being unbalanced — so a later posting reusing the id is rejected as a duplicate; the duplicate check runs BEFORE the balance/line-count check, so a duplicate id is rejected once for duplication rather than evaluated again
unresolved_intent.rationale: The spec says a duplicate is an id 'already accepted or rejected earlier in the batch', which requires seen-tracking to include rejections; ordering the duplicate check first keeps a single rejection reason per posting and makes the outcome independent of whether the repeat is balanced

unresolved_intent.decision: Balances are emitted as a JSON object built from a plain dict in first-touch insertion order (Python 3.7+ dicts preserve insertion order); keys are not sorted and no separators/indent options are set
unresolved_intent.rationale: The spec explicitly leaves output formatting unfixed and constrains only structure and values, so the cheapest deterministic order — the order accounts are first touched by accepted postings — is used rather than inventing a sort contract

unresolved_intent.decision: An account whose accepted lines net to 0 (including an account touched only by zero-amount lines) still appears in balances with value 0; accounts are pruned only when every posting touching them was rejected
unresolved_intent.rationale: The spec states balances include every account appearing in at least one ACCEPTED posting and that zero-amount lines legally 'touch the account with 0', so presence is decided by acceptance, not by the resulting value

unresolved_intent.decision: ERROR is printed to standard output (not stderr) and the process exits 0 via normal return from main(); malformed UTF-8 or unparseable JSON, a non-list top level, a non-object element, and missing or mistyped id/lines/account/amount all collapse to the same single ERROR line for the whole input, with no partial results emitted
unresolved_intent.rationale: The contract requires one line on stdout and exit 0 in all cases, and states shape problems fail the whole input, so no per-posting error reporting or nonzero exit code is introduced

unresolved_intent.decision: Unknown extra keys on a posting object or a line object are ignored rather than treated as shape violations
unresolved_intent.rationale: The acceptance criterion enumerates shape problems as missing or mistyped required fields; rejecting unlisted extras would add a strictness the spec never asked for and would make the format non-extensible
